Left: the FAE lineage in a force-directed layout of the joint (WNN) graph; stem-like FAE cells branch into FAE enterocytes and M cells. Click a state in the legend to hide it; double-click to show it alone. Right: marker genes across the states.
DynaVelo RNA velocity
DynaVelo motif velocity
DynaVelo-predicted velocities projected onto the FAE lineage layout (crypt ISCs excluded). Streamlines show the direction in which cells are moving on the graph; points are colored by state. Left: RNA velocity. Right (button): motif accessibility velocity.
Gene programs: predicted expression
Motif programs: predicted accessibility
Genome-wide view of the two branches, from DynaVelo-predicted values (crypt ISCs excluded). Rows are genes (left) or motifs (button), grouped into modules and ordered by where they peak; columns are pseudotime bins along the shared trunk and then each branch. Each row is z-scored across the trunk and both branches. Gene modules come from the fate analysis. Motif modules (247 motifs, 6 modules) come from hierarchical clustering of accessibility profiles and are named by their top motifs.
Fate probability: combined RNA and motif velocity
Fate probability: RNA velocity
Fate probability: motif velocity
Fate probability: pseudotime-based
Probability that each cell reaches the M cell fate (CellRank; terminal states are M cells, late and FAE enterocytes), against diffusion pseudotime from the most stem-like FAE cell. The grey band is the shared trunk. Cells in the terminal states sit at 0 or 1 by construction, and the plateau near 0.65 in early cells reflects the kernel and terminal-state setup, not an early M cell bias. Use the buttons to compare fate probabilities from combined, RNA velocity, motif velocity and pseudotime-based kernels.
Shared TFs: FAE enterocyte path
Shared TFs: M cell path
Shared TFs: both paths
TFs whose expression changes by a similar amount on both paths. Rows are ordered by when motif accessibility turns on. Columns are eight pseudotime bins from stem-like FAE to the end of the path; the colored strip shows the dominant state in each bin. Motif accessibility is z-scored and RNA scaled 0-1 per TF across both paths (DynaVelo-predicted values). Use the buttons to show the FAE enterocyte path, the M cell path, or both.

FAE enterocyte-biased TFs: both paths
TFs whose expression changes more on the FAE enterocyte path than on the M cell path. Rows are ordered by when motif accessibility turns on. Columns are eight pseudotime bins from stem-like FAE to the end of the path; the colored strip shows the dominant state in each bin. Motif accessibility is z-scored and RNA scaled 0-1 per TF across both paths (DynaVelo-predicted values). Use the buttons to show the FAE enterocyte path, the M cell path, or both.
